Generate initial attractivenesses from the weighted simplex

Source: R/blvim_initialise.R
blvim_simplex_initialise.Rd

This is the default generator used by blvim_initialise(). It samples initial attractivenesses from the weighted simplex $$ \sum_j \kappa_j Z_j = \sum_i X_i. $$

Usage

blvim_simplex_initialise(
  context,
  n = 10L,
  face_fraction = 0.5,
  points_per_face = 0L,
  max_partial_attempts = 1000000L,
  include_centre = TRUE
)

Arguments

context

A model context created internally by blvim().

n

Number of initial configurations to generate. The default is deliberately modest because blvim() performs one complete optimisation from each generated configuration.

face_fraction

Proportion of starting points generated on proper faces of the weighted simplex.

points_per_face

Parameter controlling the allocation of points among simplex faces. See sample_weighted_simplex().

max_partial_attempts

Maximum number of proposals used when selecting distinct faces in a partial codimension layer. See sample_weighted_simplex().

include_centre

Whether to include the centre of the weighted simplex as the first starting point. If TRUE, n - 1 points are sampled and the centre is prepended. Thus, the returned matrix always has n rows.

Value

a list containing:

  • Z: the matrix of initial attractivenesses;

  • sampling: diagnostics returned by sample_weighted_simplex(), or NULL when no random point is requested.

See also

blvim_initialise(), sample_weighted_simplex(), blvim()

Examples

distances <- french_cities_distances[1:10, 1:10] / 1000
production <- rep(1, 10)
# Emphasise proper faces of the simplex
boundary_initialise <- blvim_initialise(
  generator = blvim_simplex_initialise,
  n = 100,
  face_fraction = 0.8,
  points_per_face = 5
)
multistart_flows <- blvim(
  distances, production, 1.5, 1 / 100,
  Z = boundary_initialise,
  algorithm = "gradient",
  keep_runs = TRUE
)
head(sim_logs(multistart_flows))
